solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Annoyed supporters of Feds rioted

parts.note: bras are garments that support

indicators.note: running riot throws the letters of the following words into disorder

explanation.surface: Fans of the federal agents running wild and getting fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The stored clue had lost its last words; the blog's hint shows the anagram of 'of Feds', signalled by 'rioted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassed off is British slang for fed up or irritated.

clue.text: Rolls spaghetti bolognese out — note the eggs/oil blending before separation

indicators.note: signals that some letters are taken out of the dish's name
the letters are mixed together, as in an emulsion, before some are separated off

parts.note: taken as written as the pool of letters
taken as written as the letters to be removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A cook mixing an emulsion of eggs and oil, with bread rolls standing in for the pasta dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of NOTE THE EGGS OIL out of SPAGHETTI BOLOGNESE; the four left over, S, P, A and B, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Baps are soft, round bread rolls, a common British term for a bun.

clue.text: Do I have the capacity to be pleasant?

definitions.meaning: a question asking whether one can manage something

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they have it in them to be nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable describes a friendly, good-natured person, a close synonym of pleasant.

clue.text: Wilder work; look the time is changing

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An urging to check the clock because the hour is moving on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilder' looks like a comparative of wild, but it is Billy Wilder, the film director.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1959 comedy film directed by Billy Wilder, starring Marilyn Monroe, is an example of his work.

clue.text: Troubled sad priest almost gives up hope

indicators.note: a troubled state is disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the final letter of the phrase sad priest is dropped

explanation.surface: A cleric in a dark mood who is close to losing faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the last letter T of SAD PRIEST, and 'Troubled' rearranges the remaining SADPRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all expectation, the same as giving up hope.

clue.text: Experienced cast

definitions.meaning: as a verb, came upon or met with
to cast metal is to ... it, melting and moulding it

explanation.definitionFit: Found means met with, and also to make by pouring molten metal into a mould, as in a foundry.

clue.text: Reptile protects its own head at the earliest opportunity

indicators.note: the reptile wraps round and shields the other piece

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
the first letter of the reptile's name

explanation.surface: A snake guarding its head at the first chance it gets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its own head' is the A that starts ASP; 'protects' places it inside ASP.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for 'as soon as possible', meaning without delay.

clue.text: Joins together again to turn over very difficult question

indicators.note: the word for rejoining is read backwards

parts.note: reknits, as broken bones or wool are knitted again

explanation.surface: Mending something only to flip it, leading to a tricky puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' reverses REKNITS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is informal for something very hard or unpleasant, such as a tough exam question.

clue.text: First of punk generation's act before the Queen is a thriller

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word punk

parts.note: a generation is an age
a turn is a performer's act on stage
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A punk-era stage show winning out over royalty as an exciting spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: TURN is a music-hall act; ER is the late Queen's royal cypher.
explanation.definitionFit: A book so gripping that the reader keeps turning pages is the sort of thing a thriller is.

clue.text: At the outset Pyrrhus rushed in and murdered Trojan king

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: Pyrrhus, son of Achilles, storming in and killing the king of Troy, as in the legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the actual legend: Pyrrhus (Neoptolemus) killed Troy's king at the fall of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the last ruler of Troy in Homer's Iliad, father of Hector and Paris.

clue.text: Illegally importing drink subsumes attack by government

indicators.note: the drink takes the other pieces inside itself

parts.note: a sling is a cocktail, as in Singapore sling
to mug is to assault and rob

explanation.surface: Bringing in contraband liquor while the state launches an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link joining the attack to government inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Smuggling is moving goods across a border secretly to avoid duties or bans.

clue.text: Greeting expanded mg cryptically

parts.note: G, short for good, comes after M, short for meridiem, that is noon

explanation.surface: An abbreviation like milligrams being spelled out as a hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expanded ... cryptically' tells you to read the letters as a picture: G follows M.
explanation.definitionFit: A salutation used to say hello between midday and evening.

clue.text: Local Stoke band loses nothing playing in this type of joint

indicators.note: the band's name is played about with into a new order
one letter is dropped from the band's name

parts.note: zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A group from Stoke-on-Trent dropping out of a gig at a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses nothing' removes one O from LOCAL STOKE BAND; 'playing' rearranges the rest. 'Joint' suggests a nightclub but is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip or shoulder is a joint where a rounded end sits in a cup, allowing movement in all directions.

clue.text: Tory involved in stoical manoeuvring. One attacks traditional ideas

indicators.note: the Tory goes into the middle of the other piece
the letters of stoical are moved around

parts.note: CON, short for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Conservative caught up in calm political scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' makes IOCLAST, and 'involved in' places the Tory just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast is a person who challenges cherished beliefs, originally a smasher of religious images.

clue.text: Monitors draughts in New England?

definitions.meaning: people or things that check, inspect or keep watch
the board game draughts is called by another name in the US, New England being a region of it

explanation.definitionFit: Checkers are people who inspect, and the American name for the board game of draughts.

clue.text: Female frame is more beautiful

parts.note: an airer is a frame for drying clothes

explanation.surface: A woman's figure being judged the prettier one.
explanation.walkthrough: An airer is a folding rack for drying laundry, common in British homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair once meant beautiful, so its comparative means lovelier.

clue.text: Full of rapture heart of austere ascetic is transformed

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new arrangement
the central letter of the word austere

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strict self-denying hermit suddenly overcome with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of AUSTERE is T; T plus ASCETIC is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overwhelmed with joy or delight, the same as rapturous.

clue.text: Scandinavian kronor dictate taking a 50/50 split

indicators.note: half of each of the two words is taken, the back half of one and the front half of the other

explanation.surface: Swedish currency imposing an even division of money.
explanation.walkthrough: NOR is the second half of KRONOR and DIC the first half of DICTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic refers to the countries of northern Europe, including the Scandinavian ones.

clue.text: Crawler. It moves at a fast pace

definitions.meaning: a snake, a creature that crawls

definitions.text: It moves at a fast pace
definitions.meaning: informal for something that goes quickly, a speedy vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A rattler is a rattlesnake, and also slang for a fast-moving thing such as a train.

clue.text: I abandoned Corfe site's redevelopment without penalty

indicators.note: the remaining letters are rebuilt in a new order
the letter I is left out of the following words

explanation.surface: A developer walking away from a project at Corfe Castle in Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I abandoned' drops I from CORFE SITE; 'redevelopment' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to escape unpunished; a scot was an old tax.

clue.text: Further concede inclusion of notice in terms of reference

indicators.note: the notice is included inside the other piece

parts.note: a remit is the scope of a task
an ad, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A further admission written into an official brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms of reference' looks like part of the definition but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit is to acknowledge again, as in conceding a point a second time.

clue.text: Hear chaps are among volunteers in school locality

parts.note: to catch a remark is to hear it
men

indicators.note: the word are sits inside the volunteers

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: Listening to fellows who help out at a local school.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The district from which a school draws its pupils is the area it serves.

clue.text: Dropsy 'became debilitating' — internal evidence seen in retrospect

indicators.note: the letters are looked at backwards
the letters lie inside the quoted words

explanation.surface: A medical record noting that a swelling condition had weakened a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: AMEDE sits inside 'became debilitating'; 'seen in retrospect' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is the old name for a swelling caused by fluid build-up, now called by this medical term (US spelling).

clue.text: Poetry's not very Gaelic

indicators.note: the following letter is left out

parts.note: poetry is verse

explanation.surface: A claim that Gaelic verse is not very good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' drops V from VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: Central characters in rally vote cemented ground for cultivation

indicators.note: takes the middle letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A political rally where the vote sealed the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The centres are ALL, OT and the middle four of CEMENTED, MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a rented plot for growing vegetables, common in Britain.

clue.text: Gold-coloured foreign sea shell

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A golden seashell found by a foreign shore.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is an abalone, a shellfish of the Channel Islands with an ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: Deserter returned to northern lake

indicators.note: the word for deserter goes backwards

parts.note: a rat deserts a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A runaway coming back to a lake in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Shortened timber surrounds long solid small verandah

indicators.note: the cut timber goes around the other pieces
the last letter of the timber word is cut off

parts.note: a batten is a strip of timber
a cone is a geometric solid

explanation.surface: A cut-down beam being fitted around a sturdy little porch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened' cuts BATTEN to BATTE, which 'surrounds' L and CONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A balconette is a small false balcony, a sort of mini verandah outside a window.
